title: High-throughput Wastewater SARS-CoV-2 Detection Pipeline
author: Caroline H Sheikhzadeh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bshvnb66
materials: Once the correct protocol is loaded, Press [START]. The KingFisher will show prompts for when to load each plate in the following order (press [START] after loading each plate to move to the next step). Machinery Check: Ensure that the correct Extraction Protocol is loaded into the KingFisher machine. Ensure that the magnetic attachment of the KingFisher is a 96 well attachment (If there is another magnetic attachment, please see Section 5 to change it). Ensure that the heating block (the piece on the bottom of the machine located beneath the magnet) is the 96 well heating block. To change the heating block refer to this link: [thermo fisher website/video link] Empty 96-well Plate + 96-well Tip Combs Elution Plate Ethanol Plate 1 Ethanol Plate 2 Wash Plate 1 Wash Plate 2 Sample Plate Ensure that each plate is oriented with the A1 well in the top right corner of the plate holder in the KingFisher. Before loading each plate, double-check that all the wells in the given plate correspond to samples in the sample plate (especially if you are running less than 96 samples).

Elution Plate 1. Load Elution Solution into a reservoir 2. Add 50 µL of MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Elution Buffer Thermo Fisher Catalog #A42364 per well to each of the Elution Plate’s columns using an 8 channel multi-channel pipette. When finished loading the wash buffer and ethanol plates, seal and prepare the sample plate before loading into the KingFisher.

Sample Plate 1. Load Binding Beads into a reservoir by doing Method 1 (prior to adding sample): Load the correct ratio of binding beads to binding solution into a reservoir with Binding Solution, so that there is 550 µL of MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Binding Solution Thermo Fisher Catalog #A42359 & 20 µL of MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Binding Beads Thermo Fisher Catalog #A42362 per well. Add 570 µL, Binding Solution + Beads Mix per well to each of the columns of the Sample Plate using an 8 channel multi-channel pipette. Method 2 (prior to adding sample): Load Binding Solution into a reservoir. Add 550 µL, binding solution per well to eacper well to each of the Sample Plate’s columns using an 8 channel multi-channel pipette. Add 20 µL, binding beads to each well from the original bottle using a single channel pipette or the 8 channel multichannel pipette with only two pipette tips (two wells at a time). 2. Add 450 µL, concentrated wastewater sample per well (from the 24-well Elution Plate) to the 96-well Sample Plate.

Mastermix preparation for a 10 µL reaction volume using the Promega SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR Kit for Wastewater (Cat.no. CS317402), is as follows: A B C 1 RT-qPCR Reaction Master Mix 1X (10 uL Reaction Volume) 100 X (100 Reactions) 2 GoTaq WW Master Mix (2X) 5 uL 500 uL 3 GoScript RT (50X) 0.2 uL 20 uL 4 20X Prime/Probe/IAC Mix 0.5 uL 50 uL 5 Nuclease Free Water 0.3 uL 30 uL [Insert names of Reagents with ca talog numbers] The presence of RT-qPCR reaction inhibitors is commonly encountered in wastewater matrices (especially those that have a higher degree of solids) and in order to screen for inhibitors. To detect inhibition specific to sewage samples, the positive control RNA ladder was run with every qPCR run (5 1:10 serial dilutions of a positive control). If Cq values for the no dilution to 1:100000 dilution are not significantly different, then PCR inhibition in the RNA extracts is unlikely. Two-tailed t-tests at a 95% confidence interval can be used to determine if the average Cq values are statistically significant from the spiked-in water control. RT-qPCR reactions were run using Promega SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR Kit for Wastewater (Cat.no. CS317402, Promega, USA). Primer/probe sets targeting the N1, N2, E gene; primers detecting Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as an internal process control; and an internal amplification control, IAC (for inhibition assessment) were used. This step for preparing the mastermix can be done using an EpMotion auto-pipetter. The following images show the proper setup.

steps.title: Sanitize BSC and prepare plates
steps.instruction: Wipe all surfaces inside the biosafety cabinet (BSL‑2+) with 70 % ethanol and RNase‑free spray, bleach any remaining samples, then turn on the UV light for 20 minutes. Inside the cabinet set up three 24‑well plates: two identical Sample Plates and one Elution Plate.

steps.title: Create sample plate map
steps.instruction: In Excel draft a plate map linking sample ID numbers to wells, then arrange the wastewater bottles so that the samples placed in the Sample Plates will match the map.

steps.title: Add Nanotrap particles
steps.instruction: Dispense 75 µL of Nanotrap Magnetic Virus Particles (Ceres Nano Catalog #44202) into every well of both 24‑well Sample Plates.

steps.title: Add wastewater to sample plates
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette draw 10 mL of wastewater, then add 5 mL of this sample to each well of the duplicate 24‑well Sample Plates. Seal the plates until they are taken to the KingFisher.

steps.title: Add MagMAX lysis solution
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of MagMAX™ Microbiome Lysis Solution (Thermo Fisher Catalog #A42361) to each well of the Elution Plate and seal it together with the sealed Sample Plates.

steps.title: Load plates into KingFisher
steps.instruction: Place an empty 24‑well plate with tip combs, then the two Sample Plates, and finally the Elution Plate (A1 well must be in the top‑right corner) into the KingFisher. Verify that all wells of the Elution Plate contain lysis buffer, especially if fewer than 24 samples are run. Load the specific Concentration Protocol file, confirm the 24‑well magnetic attachment, and press [Start] after each plate is loaded.

substeps.instruction: Load protocol file and magnetic attachment

steps.title: Run KingFisher concentration
steps.instruction: Execute the loaded protocol; the run lasts approximately 00:53:00. After completion the Elution Plate contains lysed sample, while the two Sample Plates and tip combs are discarded as biohazard waste.

steps.title: Collect wastewater via autosampler
steps.instruction: Wear two face masks, double gloves, a face shield, and a lab gown; spray all PPE with 70 % ethanol and discard as biohazard after use. Stop the autosampler program (Run/Halt → Down Arrow → “Stop Program” → Select). Unclip the three lid clips, then the three middle‑section clips, lift the middle section, and remove the full 1 L Nalgene bottle (held by a partner). Unscrew the bottle, replace it with a clean capped bottle, spray the full bottle with 70 % ethanol, and re‑attach. Re‑align the clips, press Run/Halt → Select to start the program, allow the pump to purge and resume drawing wastewater, then replace the top cover.

substeps.instruction: Lift middle section and remove bottle
Unscrew and replace bottle with clean one

steps.title: Disinfect and dispose raw samples
steps.instruction: Add concentrated bleach to the remaining raw sewage in the collection bottle to reach a final sodium hypochlorite concentration of 10 % (v/v); mix and let stand for 30 minutes. Dispose of the disinfected waste according to EHS guidelines. Rinse the bottles with water, soak in 5 % HCl in DI water, wash in a bottle washer, and heat‑sterilize before next use.

steps.title: Gather extraction plates and reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare five 96‑well plates (four for washes/ethanol, one Sample Plate) and one 96‑well Elution Plate. Gather the following reagents: 80 % ethanol; MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Wash Solution (Catalog #A42360); MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Binding Solution (Catalog #A42359); MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Binding Beads (Catalog #A42362); MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Elution Buffer (Catalog #A42364).

steps.title: Label and load plates into EpMotion
steps.instruction: Label all five 96‑well plates and the Elution Plate. Load them into the EpMotion in this order: Sample Plate, Wash Buffer Plate 1, Wash Buffer Plate 2, Ethanol Plate 1, Ethanol Plate 2. Also label five reservoirs for 80 % ethanol, Wash Buffer, Binding Solution + Beads, and Elution Buffer, and load them into the EpMotion.

steps.title: Prepare ethanol and wash plates
steps.instruction: Load 80 % ethanol into a reservoir and dispense 1 mL of ethanol into each well of both Ethanol Plates using an 8‑channel pipette. Load Wash Buffer into another reservoir and dispense 1 mL of MagMAX™ Viral/Pathogen Wash Solution (Catalog #A42360) into each well of both Wash Plates using an 8‑channel pipette.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 1 mL ethanol per well of Ethanol Plate 1
Dispense 1 mL ethanol per well of Ethanol Plate 2
Dispense 1 mL wash buffer per well of Wash Plate 1
Dispense 1 mL wash buffer per well of Wash Plate 2

steps.title: Transfer concentrated sample to 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: From the 24‑well Elution Plate, pipette 450 µL of concentrated wastewater into the corresponding well of the 96‑well Sample Plate (1:1 mapping according to the Extraction Plate Map). Change tips between each sample to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Run EpMotion extraction program
steps.instruction: Start the EpMotion extraction protocol, which adds Binding Solution + Beads, performs wash steps with Wash Buffer and 80 % ethanol, and finally elutes nucleic acid into the Elution Plate. The program runs automatically to completion (≈ 00:35:00).

steps.title: Run KingFisher extraction
steps.instruction: Load the Elution Plate (now containing bound nucleic acid) into the KingFisher with the 24‑well magnetic attachment, select the Extraction Protocol file, and press [Start]. The run lasts approximately 00:35:00. After completion the Elution Plate contains purified nucleic acid.

steps.title: Seal elution plate and discard consumables
steps.instruction: Seal the Elution Plate for downstream PCR. Discard the Sample, Wash, Ethanol plates and tip combs in plastic waste after emptying their contents into a separate biohazard waste container.

steps.title: Set up multiplex RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet prepare a 384‑well qPCR plate. Add 4 µL of each eluted sample and 6 µL of mastermix to achieve a 10 µL reaction volume per well (use EpMotion or manual pipette). Seal the plate with a thermal seal and centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Run qPCR and interpret results
steps.instruction: Run the plate on a Bio‑Rad CFX384 Touch (catalog #1855484) selecting ‘All Channels’. Use fluorophores: FAM for N1, N2, E (SARS‑CoV‑2); HEX/JOE for internal amplification control; ROX/CXR for reference dye; Cy5 for PMMoV. Quantify SARS‑CoV‑2 RNA using a standard curve of nine‑fold serial dilutions (linear regression y = mx + b, slope ≈ –3.3). If the IAC Ct shifts >3 Ct versus NTC or fails to amplify, consider the result invalid and repeat nucleic‑acid purification.
